In his first book he wrote about a Princeton basketball player who embodied "all the possibilities of the game [he] had ever imagined. In addition to Levels of the Game and his profile of Bill (*) Bradley in A Sense of Where You Are, he examined Florida's citrus industry in Oranges and Theodore Taylor's work on the Manhattan and Orion Projects in The Curve of Binding Energy. 3.q: His left shoulder bears a tattoo showing a bearded, blue-robed man holding a staff and extending spindly hands over the tool of this man's trade, all underneath the word "Poohdini." His brother Reggie coached his AAU team, Mean Street Express, which also included future NBA-er Eric Gordon. He led the Simeon Career Academy to two straight state titles in Illinois. They lost the 1983 AFC Championship Game to the Raiders under first-year head coach Chuck Knox, and Jim Zorn was the starting quarterback for this team's first game. 3.q: A key pass thrown to Randy Peschel cost this school "The Big Shootout" game, which saw President Richard Nixon watch this team, then coached by Frank Broyles, lose to the Darrell Royal-led Texas. Later, as Athletic Director, Broyles would face racial discrimination charges from the men's basketball coach at this school who took the team to the 1995 NCAA championship game, losing to UCLA despite employing Nolan (*) Richardson's "40 Minutes of Hell" strategy. True freshman quarterback Mitch Mustain helped lead this team to the SEC Championship game in 2006, but transferred after the season after being benched by then-coach Huston Nutt. Currently facing controversy over rape allegations involving five members of the men's basketball team, FTP, name this alma mater of Felix Jones and Darren McFadden, an SEC school and popularizer of the WildHog formation.

This team made the playoffs in its first year of existence despite its tragic loss of Bill Masterton, who became the only player to die during an NHL game. One player who played for this team in between two stints for the Rangers is known for committing an infamous face-to-face screen against Martin Brodeur. The personal lives of Los Angeles's Jarret Stoll and Calgary's Dion Phaneuf led to the termination of that player's career with this franchise, after he referred to ex-girlfriends Rachel Hunter and Elisha Cuthbert as (*) "sloppy seconds." This team, which suspended Sean Avery in 2008, relocated in 1993and dropped the word "north" from their name. One player on this team was the second American to reach 500 goals, while this team's only Stanley Cup victory came in 1999 when Brett Hull scored a controversial goal against the Buffalo Sabres. Marc Crawford became this team's coach in 2009, succeeding Dave Tippet. FTP, name this team whose current captain is Brennen Morrow and whose past talent includes Mike Modano, an NHL team based out of a city whose other sports franchises include the Mavericks and the Cowboys.

Mark Taylor's first international test match as captain was against this country, in which this country won by one wicket on the final day. In a match between this country and India in 1999, Anil Kumble ("COOM-blay") took all ten wickets in a single innings, finishing 10-74 ("10 for 74"). David Warner scored 335 not out against this country in 2019, and Zak Crawley's top score in professional cricket was a score of (*) 267 against this country. A test match series against this country featured both Will Jacks and Rehan ("RAY-an") Ahmed taking 5-fors on debut, as well as Harry Brook scoring his first three test match centuries. England beat this country in the final of the 2022 T20 World Cup. For 10 points, name this country, nicknamed the Men in Green, whose players include Babar Azam and Shaheen Shah Afridi.

A player for this team refused to sign his contract until he became the halftime accordion performer. This team sent an ice skating show to Rochester, New York to convince the Rochester Royals to draft Si Green instead of their second pick in the 1956 NBA draft. Another player for this team suffered back pain for the rest of his career after building his mother a driveway. A player for this team from the University of San Francisco was the first (*) Black coach to win an NBA championship while also being a player. The number 6 was retired league-wide in 2022 following the death of that former player for this team. The first "big three" era of this team featured a sharpshooter nicknamed "The Hick from French Lick." For 10 points, name this NBA team whose players have included Bill Russell, Larry Bird, and Jayson Tatum.

Joe Roth played for this school for the entire 1976 season despite being diagnosed with melanoma. During a bowl game between Georgia Tech and this school, Benny Lom attempted to stop Roy Riegels from running the wrong way after a recovered fumble. Joe Starkey remarked, "I have never, never seen anything like it," after Kevin Moen scored a touchdown for this school after five controversial lateral passes. This school won a (*) 1982 rivalry game on that last-second kickoff return often called "The Play," despite the opposing team's marching band storming the field too early. The Axe is contested in the "Big Game" between this school and a southerly rival, who both joined the ACC after leaving the PAC-12. For 10 points, name this home of the Golden Bears, a rival of Stanford.
3.r: California Golden Bears [or Cal; or UC Berkeley; accept Golden Bears until read]

3.q: Aubrey Plaza once had an awkward encounter with this professional athlete, in which she pretended to be a makeup artist and allegedly did his hair. In one SNL sketch, Jay Pharaoh did a Stephen A. Smith impression where he said that this athlete should be locked in a small closet "where there are no basketballs or round objects of any kind." This athlete urged kids to learn computer science in an op-ed for Wired titled "Here's Why You Should Learn to Code."NBA 2K16 replicated an instance in which this player photobombed his teammate by suddenly (*) rising into view of the camera, eclipsing his teammate's interview.This player was the fourth pick in the NBA draft in 2003, when he left Georgia Tech to become the center of a team that later included Andrea Bargnani and DeMar DeRozan. For 10 points, name this NBA player who played for the Toronto Raptors before joining Dwyane Wade and Lebron James in the Miami Heat's "Big 3."

A former NBA all-star for this team coached Deanna Nolan for most of her career on a WNBA team in the same city after being hired during Swin Cash's rookie season. A former NBA All-Star for this team won three WNBA titles in the 2000s with the Shock and preceded Becky Hammon as Aces head coach. A former player for this NBA team was hired as the Pelicans' GM in 2025. In 2004, this team starred both Ben Wallace and (*) Rasheed Wallace on a defensive juggernaut that beat the Shaq-Kobe ("koh-bee") Lakers in the NBA finals. In the 2003 draft, this team followed LeBron's pick by passing over Carmelo Anthony in favor of Serbian center Darko Milicic ("MILL-ih-chitch"). For 10 points, Joe Dumars and Isiah Thomas played for the "Bad Boys" on what midwestern NBA team?

In a playoff game, a batter for this team was struck out on a fake intentional walk by Rollie Fingers. A catcher who spent most of the 1930s with this team is the favorite baseball player of American Girl's Kit Kittredge; that catcher also caught Johnny Vander Meer's back-to-back no-hitters with this team. In 1970, a player on this team scored the winning run of the MLB All-Star Game by running over and injuring catcher (*) Ray Fosse. The leader among catchers in baseball-reference WAR played his entire career for this team while playing alongside early-career Tony Perez. Johnny Bench played for this team, which in the 2010s starred Canadian catcher-turned-first baseman Joey Votto. For 10 points, Elly De La Cruz plays for what MLB team based in a city in southern Ohio?

It's not football, but the oldest surviving equipment for this sport is housed in the Stirling Smith Art Gallery and Museum. The Tournament of Hearts, commonly referred to as the Scotties, is a competition in this sport. Under the captaincy of Thomas Ulsrud, the Norwegian men's team in this sport attracted attention for wearing trousers with unusual patterns. The (*) projectiles used in this sport are typically fitted with an "eye on the hog", which ensures the projectile's release before thehog line. Great Britain's only medals at the 2022 Winter Olympics came in this sport. In this sport, the team going last is said to have the hammer, with the target being known as the house. For 10 points, name this winter sport in which stones are slid on ice towards a circular target.

In a 4-0 defeat to Chelsea in 2013, a player for this team missed a penalty and scored two own goals. In 2008, Robin van Persie was shown a red card for shoulder-barging this team's goalkeeper. The fastest goal by a goalkeeper in Premier League history was scored for this team after 14 seconds in a match against Southampton. This team beat Liverpool (*) 6-1 in Steven Gerrard's final Premier League match. This club suffered their only Premier League relegation in 2018 before Liverpool signed Xherdan Shaqiri. In a debate about Messi and Ronaldo in 2010, Andy Gray coined the phrase "can they do it on a cold, rainy night [against this team]". After joining the Premier League in 2008, this team were known for long throws taken by Rory Delap. For 10 points, the Bet365 stadium is home to which West Midlands team, known as the Potters?
